ips.q: What is an IPS QR code?
ips.a: IPS QR is the National Bank of Serbia standard for instant payments. The code contains the recipient account, amount, payment code, purpose and reference, so nobody has to type them by hand.

pay.q: How do I pay with the QR code?
pay.a: Open your mobile banking app, choose “IPS scan” or “Pay with QR”, and scan the code from the screen or the printed slip. Check the details and confirm.

privacy.a: No. The slip and QR code are generated in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server; the draft is saved only on your device.

model.q: What are model 97 and the reference number?
model.a: The reference number (poziv na broj) lets the recipient match your payment. Model 97 means the first two digits of the reference are check digits. For taxes and fees, copy the model and reference from the tax notice or the institution's website.

code.q: Which payment code should I choose?
code.a: The first digit is the payment form (1 cash, 2 non-cash), the other two are the basis. Personal bills usually use 89, taxes and fees 53, utilities 22.

kinds.q: What is the difference between a payment slip and a transfer order?
kinds.a: A payment slip (nalog za uplatu) is for cash payments at a bank or post office. A transfer order (nalog za prenos) is for paying from your own account and also includes the debtor account.

share.q: How do I send a filled slip to someone?
share.a: Fill in the slip and click “Share link”. The link is copied, and on a phone the share menu opens (Viber, WhatsApp, Telegram). The recipient opens the same slip with its QR code and can pay right away.

cyrillic.q: Can I print the slip in Cyrillic?
cyrillic.a: Yes. Choose “ћирилица” above the slip and its labels switch to Cyrillic. You can type the details in either script.

batch.q: How do I print several slips at once?
batch.a: Fill in a slip and click “Add to batch”, then change the details for the next one. When you are done, “Download PDF” makes one file with three slips per A4 page and cut lines.

model97.metaTitle: Model 97 calculator: check digits for reference numbers
model97.metaDescription: Compute model 97 check digits for a Serbian payment reference (poziv na broj) and verify an existing one. Free and instant.
model97.title: Model 97: check digit calculator
model97.lead: Enter the reference number without check digits and get the full number ready for the slip. Or verify an existing one.
model97.bodyLabel: Reference without the first two digits
model97.bodyHint: Digits only; dashes and spaces are ignored
model97.bad: Check digits are wrong. For this number they should be {control}.
model97.howTitle: How model 97 check digits are computed
model97.how1: Model 97 uses ISO 7064 (MOD 97-10). The check digits are the first two digits of the reference.
model97.step1: Take the reference body (without check digits) and append 00.
model97.step2: Find the remainder of that number divided by 97.
model97.step4: Pad a single-digit result with a leading zero. Those are the first two digits of the reference.
model97.example: Example: for the body 3220000111111111000 the check digits are 16, so the reference is 163220000111111111000.

what.a: The model is a two-digit code in front of the reference number. Model 97 means the reference contains check digits, so the bank can catch a typo before money goes to the wrong payment.

where.a: Mostly for public revenue: taxes, fees, contributions and fines. You usually get the reference in the tax notice, or the institution builds it, e.g. from a municipality code and your ID number.

letters.q: What if the reference has letters?
letters.a: The standard converts letters to numbers (A = 10 … Z = 35), but Serbian public payments use digits only. This calculator works with digits.

codesPage.metaDescription: All payment codes for Serbian payment slips: what 189, 289, 253, 254, 221 mean and when to use 1 or 2 as the first digit. Search by number or text.
codesPage.title: Payment codes (šifre plaćanja)
codesPage.lead: A payment code has three digits. The first is the payment form, the other two are the basis of payment. Find the right code by number or description.

first.q: What does the first digit of the payment code mean?
first.a: 1 means cash, e.g. paying at a post office or bank counter. 2 means non-cash payment from an account, via e-banking or IPS QR. 3 is used for settlement payments such as offsetting.

which.q: Which code do I use for bills, rent or taxes?
which.a: Individuals use 289 (or 189 at the counter). Companies and sole traders must not use 189/289 and pick the code for the actual basis. Taxes, fees and fines use 253, withholding taxes 254, rent 226, utilities 222.

wrong.q: What if I use the wrong payment code?
wrong.a: The payment usually still arrives, because the bank and the recipient match it by account and reference number. The code is used for statistics and records, but for public revenue it is better to use the exact one.

codesPage.source: Source: NBS decision on payment order forms, Annex 3

format.q: What does a Serbian account number look like?
format.a: It has 18 digits: three for the bank, thirteen for the account and two check digits. It is often written short, without leading zeros in the middle part, e.g. 160-5100000000-02.

control.a: The last two digits are computed with mod 97 from the first sixteen. One wrong digit breaks the check, and the bank rejects the order.

bank.q: How do I find out which bank an account belongs to?
bank.a: The first three digits are the bank code assigned by the National Bank of Serbia. This page shows the bank automatically.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.metaDescription: How Uplatnica handles data: the slip draft stays in your browser and nothing is sent to a server.
privacy.data: The slip details (payee, account, amount, reference) stay in your browser. The draft, the print batch and the chosen language are kept only in localStorage on your device. The site sends none of it to a server and has no accounts or database. Clearing the site data in your browser deletes it.
privacy.analytics: Visits are counted with Plausible: no cookies, no personal data and no tracking across sites.
privacy.ads: The site shows ads through Google AdSense. Google and its partners may use cookies and similar technologies to show and measure ads. You manage consent through Google's consent message.
privacy.adsLink: How Google uses data from partner sites
privacy.donate: Donations go directly to the listed payment providers and bank. The site does not process them and keeps no data about donors.

howTo.title: How to fill in a Serbian payment slip
howTo.templateTitle: How to fill in this slip

payer.title: Payer and purpose
payer.text: Write the name and address of whoever pays, up to three lines, and briefly what the payment is for. The IPS QR code holds up to 70 characters for the payer and 35 for the purpose.

payee.title: Recipient
payee.text: Name and seat of the recipient, as written on the invoice, decision or the institution's website.

code.title: Payment code
code.text: Three digits: the first is the form of payment (1 cash, 2 non-cash), the other two the basis, e.g. 53 for taxes and fees. The full list is in the “Payment codes” tool.

amount.title: Currency and amount
amount.text: The currency is RSD. The amount is written with a decimal comma, e.g. 2.500,00.

account.title: Recipient account
account.text: 18 digits: three for the bank, thirteen for the account and two check digits. It may be written without leading zeros in the middle, e.g. 840-742221843-57. The generator verifies the check digits with mod 97.

reference.title: Model and reference number
reference.text: The reference number (poziv na broj) is how the recipient matches the payment. Model 97 means the first two digits of the reference are check digits. For taxes and fees take both from the decision or the institution's website; if the recipient gave none, leave the fields empty.

howTo.ipsTitle: The IPS QR code on the slip
howTo.ipsText: IPS QR is the National Bank of Serbia standard for instant payments. The code holds the recipient's account and name, the amount in dinars, the payment code, purpose and reference, and is built to the NBS recommendations for generators. In your mobile banking app you scan the code, check the details and confirm; the bank may let you change some of them, such as the amount.
